Performers
Carl Sandburg (narrator), New York Philharmonic (orchestra), André Kostelanetz (conductor) Documented

All three are explicitly credited on Columbia MS 6040. No individual orchestral players are identified.

[1] [2]
Work version
1942 work for narrator and orchestra; narration in English Documented

The LP calls it A Lincoln Portrait. This is the orchestral work, not Walter Beeler’s band transcription. The performing edition and session alterations are unknown.

[2] [4]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

1959 is the documented carrier issue year; a session date has not been established from the consulted carrier evidence.

[1] [2]
Place
Unknown Unknown

The orchestra’s name does not establish a particular studio or concert venue.

[1] [2]
Label
Columbia Masterworks Documented

US stereo vinyl LP; sleeve explicitly identifies the stereo release.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
MS 6040 Documented

Archive catalogue dates this carrier to 1959; the sleeve also carries Library of Congress catalogue numbers beginning R59.

[1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 1, band 1 Documented

The selected segmented file contains the complete Lincoln Portrait. Matrix, take and stamper identifiers are unknown.

[3] [2]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP transfer Documented

Institutional transfer credit; no independently established personal mastering credit.

[1]
Transfer date
2021-07-30 Documented

From ripping_date 20210730123604. The sleeve scan is separately dated 8 July 2021.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; segmented VBR MP3 derivative Documented

The item documents this transfer chain. Equalisation, pitch correction, noise reduction and other restoration settings are unknown.

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Copyrighted Copland composition; musical-work permissions administered by Boosey & Hawkes Documented

Lincoln’s nineteenth-century speeches and Copland’s twentieth-century musical work are distinct rights objects. No permission for republication of the complete composition or a modern score is asserted.

[4] [6]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1959, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

Under the project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule, the documented commercial carrier’s former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This includes the recorded narration as part of the phonogram assessment. It is not US or worldwide clearance, not a Creative Commons licence and not a US-government recording; composition rights remain separate.

[1] [2] [8] [7]

Aaron Copland, Lincoln Portrait; Carl Sandburg, narrator; New York Philharmonic, André Kostelanetz. Columbia Masterworks MS 6040 (1959 issue), Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Copland composition remains copyrighted.
